decision: Agree research-only non-promotion; no demonstrated historical forecast error.
read_extent: Re-read original physical pages 5–6. Read source BT14/7062 cover/financial context and physical4; BT14/7332 physical2/6; BT15/1313 physical1–2/6; BT15/1726 physical2/5; BT14/9751 physical68. No full source-law reading or every historical forecast vintage reconstructed.
checks: The original 2002–2005 differences add to EUR8.4bn. Arithmetic itself is consistent.

The cited amendment tableaux state incremental revenue effects, not a complete four-year total-revenue forecast. Converting them into totals requires an identified pre-reform baseline and matching forecast date.

BT14/9751 physical68 is explicitly the May2002 forecast. Its tabacco-revenue series is 13.1/13.5/13.8/13.9bn for2002–2005, but a later revised vintage cannot by itself disprove an earlier expectation.

The 2003 committee discussion expressly acknowledges uncertain forecasts and changes in consumer behaviour. Observed receipts versus one specified forecast would establish a forecast miss, not causal attribution solely to tax changes.
The original footnote combines multiple legislation stages and a trade-association republication. This is a source-chain limitation, not proof the synthesized total was invented or erroneous.
limits: No corrected EUR loss, counterfactual receipts, causal tax effect or intent inferred. Same original submission already screened in the baseline; no new reading unit counted.

later_disposition_cross_reference.note: The later matching reconstruction justifies a formal unresolved source-description lead. This supersedes the earlier research-only procedural disposition, but does not promote the allegation to a proven finding or erase the baseline/vintage qualifications.
